1: # DB — NEW Schema (Supabase + Drizzle)
2: 
3: Design targets (from plan): thread === workflow (1:1 after bind), chat-first,
4: PERSONAL auto workspace, MVP single-workspace (scalable), durable chat + queued
5: messages, binding approvals, plans with steps, activities/tool streaming for
6: ThinkingSteps, per-workspace API keys, mem0 thread memory, files in Supabase
7: Storage, realtime notifications, **collaboration** (workspace membership +
8: thread sharing, see ARCHITECTURE §I Permission model).
9: 
10: ## Conventions
11: - Every table: `id text primary key` (ULID via `packages/db/src/ids.ts`,
12:   prefixes `thd_`, `wf_`, `msg_`, `run_`, `pln_`, `pls_`, `apv_`, `not_`, `key_`,
13:   `fil_`, `wp_`, `grp_`, `inv_`, `tco_`, `wme_`, `alm_`), `created_at timestamptz not null default
14:   now()`, `updated_at`.
15: - All plaintext user data (API keys, secrets) NEVER stored — use Supabase Vault
16:   or encrypted column (see `workspace_api_keys`).
17: - RLS on every user table: `to authenticated using ( owner = auth.uid() )`
18:   (+ `with check` on update). Owner column is almost always `user_id`.
19: - text enums via Postgres `enum` types; drizzle maps to TS unions.
20: 
21: ## Tables
22: 
23: ### 1. `workspaces`
24: | col | type | notes |
25: |---|---|---|
26: | id | text pk | `wp_` prefix |
27: | name | text not null | e.g. "Personal" |
28: | created_by | uuid not null ref auth.users | |
29: | is_default | bool not null default false | PERSONAL per-user |
30: | created_at / updated_at | | |
31: Index: `(created_by, name)` unique.
32: RLS: owner only.
33: > MVP: auto-created "Personal" per user (is_default). Users can ALSO be added
34: > as members to OTHER workspaces via workspace invites — those workspaces show
35: > in the switcher (badge if not owner). Creating extra own-workspaces is a
36: > pro/future feature (plan limits: free = 1 owned, 3 groups, 5 threads/group).
37: 
38: ### 2. `groups`  ← sidebar folder of threads (the "group" concept)
39: | col | type | notes |
40: |---|---|---|
41: | id | text pk `grp_` |
42: | workspace_id | text ref workspaces cascade |
43: | user_id | uuid ref auth.users | creator |
44: | name | text not null | PERSONAL, SITE, WORKFLOWS, INVITES, user-created groups… |
45: | kind | enum(custom, system) default custom | system = PERSONAL/SITE/WORKFLOWS/INVITES |
46: | position | int default 0 |
47: | created_at / updated_at |
48: Unique (workspace_id, name). Indexes: (workspace_id, position).
49: RLS: owner OR member. Readable to user when owner or workspace member.
50: > **INVITES is a REAL system group** created at signup (with PERSONAL, SITE,
51: > WORKFLOWS). It is LOCKED: cannot be renamed/deleted, user cannot manually add
52: > a thread to it. It only gets populated when the user ACCEPTS a thread invite;
53: > then the owner's thread appears there. Guest cannot add anything to INVITES
54: > unless invited.
55: 
56: ### 3. `workspace_members`  ← who is in the workspace (owner/editor/viewer)
57: | col | type | notes |
58: |---|---|---|
59: | id | text pk `wme_` |
60: | workspace_id | text ref workspaces on delete cascade |
61: | user_id | uuid ref auth.users |
62: | role | enum(owner, editor, viewer) default viewer |
63: | created_at |
64: Unique (workspace_id, user_id). Creator auto-inserted as `owner` by trigger.
65: RLS: owner manages (CUD); members SELECT.
66: > Joined workspace = access to the OWNER's real workspace (all groups + threads
67: > visible to every member). Roles: owner=full, editor=work (create/edit/run/
68: > delete any thread/group, edit plans), viewer=read-only. NO owner/admin/member.
69: 
70: ### 4. `user_profiles`
71: | col | type | notes |
72: |---|---|---|
73: | id | text pk `prf_` |
74: | user_id | uuid ref auth.users unique |
75: | onboarded | bool default false |
76: | pre_answers | jsonb | signup question answers (JSON-driven onboarding) |
77: | plan | enum(free, pro) default free |
78: | prefer_own_keys_in_shared | bool default false | profile toggle: "use my own key in invited workspaces" |
79: | created_at / updated_at |
80: RLS: `auth.uid()`. Written at signup, editable in Profile dialog.
81: 
82: ### 5. `threads`  ← chat container AND (bound) workflow
83: | col | type | notes |
84: |---|---|---|
85: | id | text pk `thd_` |
86: | workspace_id | text ref workspaces cascade |
87: | group_id | text ref groups null | which sidebar group it lives in |
88: | user_id | uuid ref auth.users | creator/owner |
89: | title | text not null default '' | auto-titled from 1st user message (smart title); rename in header input still available |
90: | deleted_at | timestamptz null | soft-archive: null = live; set on delete → recoverable 30 days, then hard-delete |

92: | bound_workflow_id | text ref workflows null | set by LLM `finalizeAndInject` tool |
93: | created_at / updated_at / last_message_at |
94: Indexes: (user_id, workspace_id, last_message_at desc); (group_id);
95: trigram or lower(title) for search.
96: RLS: owner OR workspace member OR via `thread_shares` (invitee sees it in
97: their own sidebar's INVITES system group).
98: > Thread identifies chat AND workflow (1:1). Must have at least null wf until bound.
99: > Limits: ≤5 threads per group, ≤3 groups per workspace (free plan) — enforced
100: > at insert (RPC / service), counted per workspace.
101: 
102: ### 6. `workflows`
103: | col | type | notes |
104: |---|---|---|
105: | id | text pk `wf_` |
106: | thread_id | text ref threads null | bind target (nullable pre-bind) |

119: `plans`: id `pln_`, workflow_id (unique), title, objective, summary, status
120: enum(draft, proposed, accepted, declined), created_at, updated_at.
121: `plan_steps`: id `pls_`, plan_id ref cascade, position int, title, description,

126: | col | type | notes |
127: |---|---|---|
128: | id | text pk `msg_` |
129: | thread_id | text ref threads cascade |

260: | id | text pk `fil_` |
261: | user_id | uuid |
262: | thread_id | text ref threads null |
263: | workspace_id | text ref workspaces cascade |
264: | bucket | text default 'chat-attachments' |
265: | path | text not null | storage path `{user}/{thread}/{ulid}.ext` |
266: | mime_type | text |
267: | size_bytes | bigint |
268: | compressed | bool default false |
269: | created_at |
270: RLS: owner. Storage bucket policy: authenticate (owner by path prefix `{auth.uid()}/`).
271: 
272: ### 17. `notification_webhooks` (optional future) — REMOVED from MVP, note only.
273: External webhooks folded into `notifications` + Inngest `notification/publish`,
274: existing `webhook-board`/`waitForWebhook` retired.
275: 
276: ## Enums (Postgres)
277: ```
278: role            : owner|editor|viewer          (workspace_members)
279: thread_role     : editor|viewer                (thread_shares / invites; no owner row — owner = threads.user_id)
280: plan            : free|pro
281: group_kind      : custom|system
282: invite_kind     : workspace|thread
283: invite_status   : pending|accepted|revoked|expired
284: workflow_status : waiting|planning|running|awaiting_approval|idle|paused|failed|completed
285: message_role    : user|assistant|system|tool
286: message_status  : queued|streaming|completed|failed|interrupted
287: run_status      : pending|running|sleeping|waiting|awaiting_approval|completed|failed|cancelled
288: activity_status : pending|active|complete|failed
289: activity_type   : tool|thinking|task|subtask|system
290: approval_status : pending|approved|denied
291: api_provider    : groq|anakin|mem0|image|speech|transcription|video
292: ```
293: 
294: ## Supabase specifics
295: - Migrations via `supabase migration new <name>` (imperative workflow).
296: - **Realtime**: enable on `chat_messages`, `run_activities`,
297:   `approval_requests`, `notifications` with private channels + JWT auth.
298: - **Storage bucket**: `chat-attachments` — create server-side w/ service role;
299:   dedicated policy `(storage.foldername(name))[1] = auth.uid()::text` for
300:   CUD. Policy for avatar/object keys too.
301: - **RLS policy list**:
302:   - owner-only tables: user_profiles, notifications, workspace_api_keys,
303:     files (+ own invites).
304:   - workspace-scoped: workspaces, groups, threads, workflows, plans,
305:     chat_messages, runs, run_activities, approval_requests → readable by owner
306:     OR any `workspace_members` row (all threads visible to members).
307:   - cross-workspace thread access: `threads` also readable via a matching
308:     `thread_shares` row (invitee; in their OWN workspace context / INVITES
309:     group). Never bundled into a shared-workspace read.
310:   - `workspace_api_keys`: SELECT only via `security definer` RPC
311:     `get_workspace_key(workspace_id, provider)` that validates <owner OR
312:     workspace_members> and decrypts server-side (service role decrypt NOT
313:     exposed). Member key resolution honors `user_profiles.prefer_own_keys_in_shared`
314:     → falls back to the member's OWN Personal workspace keys.
315: - **Oracle triggers**: `on_auth_user_created` → insert
316:   `workspaces(Personal)` (is_default) + `user_profiles` row +
317:   `workspace_members(owner)` for that workspace + system `groups`
318:   (PERSONAL, SITE, WORKFLOWS, INVITES — INVITES locked empty) automatically.
319: 
320: ## Why this shape (reasoning)
321: - `threads` + `workflows` split: a chat exists before any plan/bind; binding
322:   sets `threads.bound_workflow_id`. MVP single-workspace but multi-thread.
323: - `groups` = the sidebar folder concept the plan asks for (New button → new
324:   custom group; INVITES is a LOCKED system group created at signup — empty
325:   until a thread invite is accepted). Group/thread limits (≤5 threads/group,
326:   ≤3 custom groups/workspace free) enforced at insert.
327: - `invites` unified (workspace | thread) keeps one token/status/expiry flow;
328:   accept fans out to `workspace_members` or `thread_shares`.
329: - `thread_shares` = invited guests only; role editor/viewer — guests get chat/
330:   run/approve but never plan-edit/rename/re-share (owner-only rights stay on
331:   `threads.user_id`).
332: - `runs` separate from workflow status: each durable pass is auditable,
333:   replayable, cancellable; activity tables hang off `run_id`.
334: - `run_activities` replaces old `event`/`observation`/`agent_state` — shaped
335:   directly for the ThinkingSteps/ToolStep UI components and realtime push,
336:   killing the god-table smell.
337: - `chat_messages` owns history (requirement: no hardcoded mock); queue solved
338:   by `status=queued` rows — durable across page close/reload.
339: - Plain user-supplied keys isolated in ONE table (never in env, never client)
340:   → the "Agent/Environment" dialog writes here.

<content>
1: # ENV — Variables & User-Suppliable Keys
2: 
3: Three layers: **server/infra env** (Vercel/Next server, never client),
4: **user workspace keys** (entered by user in Workflow Settings → Agent/Env tab,
5: stored in DB, encrypted), and **per-thread overrides** (rare, optional).
6: 
7: ## Existing env (old backend → what to keep)
8: 
9: | Var | Used by (old) | New use |
10: |---|---|---|
11: | `DATABASE_URL` / `DIRECT_URL` | drizzle pg | → Supabase project connection string (keep, used by drizzle) |
12: | `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` / `BETTER_AUTH_URL` | better-auth | **DELETE** (Supabase Auth owns sessions) |
13: | `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` | unused today | keep — supabase-js client |
14: | `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` | unused today | keep — anon role for RLS/DATA API |
15: | `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` | — | **ADD** server-only, storage uploads + admin (never NEXT_PUBLIC) |
16: | `ANAKIN_API_KEY` / `ANAKIN_BASE_URL` | agent adapters | fallback default; user can override per workspace |
17: | `GROQ_API_KEY` / `GROQ_MODEL` | runtime | fallback defaults; per workspace override |
18: | `MEM0_API_KEY` | workflow mem0 | fallback; per workspace override |
19: | `INNGEST_EVENT_KEY` / `SIGNING_KEY` / `APP_ID` | inngest client | keep |
20: | `WEBHOOK_BASE_URL` | webhook-board | keep |
21: | `AGENT_MAX_STEPS` / `AGENT_MAX_TOOL_CALLS` / `EXECUTION_MAX_SECONDS` / `EXECUTION_MAX_COST_USD` / `EXECUTION_MAX_SLEEP_SECONDS` / `RECOVERY_MAX_ATTEMPTS` | inngest | keep as server caps (hard ceiling) |
22: 
23: ## NEW env (definitive list, final)
24: 
25: ```
26: # --- Supabase ---
27: DATABASE_URL                # postgres connection for drizzle (direct)
28: DIRECT_URL                  # pooler direct url (non-pooled, for migrations)
29: NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL    # client
30: NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY  # client anon (never secret)
31: SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY   # server only — storage bucket mgmt, user creation
32: SUPABASE_AUTH_SECRET        # optional: for verifying webhook JWT from auth hooks
33: 
34: # --- Inngest ---
35: INNGEST_EVENT_KEY
36: INNGEST_SIGNING_KEY
37: INNGEST_APP_ID
38: 
39: # --- Webhook interop ---
40: WEBHOOK_BASE_URL            # base url for generated /api/v1/hooks/:token urls
41: 
42: # --- Defaults (single fallback key each; user overrides per-workspace in UI) ---
43: ANAKIN_API_KEY
44: ANAKIN_BASE_URL             # default https://api.anakin.io/v1
45: GROQ_API_KEY
46: GROQ_MODEL                  # default text model, e.g. openai/gpt-oss-20b
47: MEM0_API_KEY
48: 
49: # --- Server hard caps (clamp user values; not editable by user) ---
50: AGENT_MAX_STEPS             # default 5      — ceiling
51: AGENT_MAX_TOOL_CALLS        # default 50     — ceiling
52: EXECUTION_MAX_SECONDS       # default 900    — ceiling
53: EXECUTION_MAX_COST_USD      # default 1      — ceiling
54: EXECUTION_MAX_SLEEP_SECONDS # default 604800 — ceiling
55: RECOVERY_MAX_ATTEMPTS       # default 2      — ceiling
56: 
57: # --- Model routing (per category; fall back from workspace → env default) ---
58: TEXT_MODEL                   # alias of GROQ_MODEL default (kept by name parity)
59: IMAGE_MODEL                  # default e.g. groq/text2img or provider, optional
60: SPEECH_MODEL                 # optional
61: TRANSCRIPTION_MODEL          # optional
62: VIDEO_MODEL                  # optional (future)
63: ```
64: 
65: > Client (`packages/env/src/web.ts`) must expose only:
66: > `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`.
67: > Everything else stays server-only. `SKIP_ENV_VALIDATION` respected.
68: 
69: ## Where the USER enters their own keys (UI)
70: 
71: Primary → **Workflow Settings dialog → "Agent" tab** (rename of
72: "Instructions"), with an **"Environment"** subsection:
73: 
74: - Groq API key + Groq model (text)
75: - Anakin API key + base URL
76: - Mem0 API key
77: - (secondary) Image / Speech / Transcription / Video model overrides
78: 
79: Stored in DB table `workspace_api_keys`:
80: `workspace_id | user_id | provider | key_name | key_value(encrypted) | created_at`.
81: 
82: Resolution order at call time:
83: ```
84: 1. member of a SHARED workspace + user_profiles.prefer_own_keys_in_shared=true
85:      → member's OWN Personal workspace keys
86: 2. workspace keys (the workspace the thread belongs to)
87: 3. env default
88: ```
89: `workflow_api_keys` optional per-thread override keyed same way (rare).
90: Encryption: AES-256-GCM with `APP_ENCRYPTION_KEY` env (add to server env) — or
91: Supabase Vault (`vault.create_secret`) if service_role available. Recommend
92: **Supabase Vault** — no extra env key, native audit.
93: 
94: > Note: ChatComposer token slider = "max tokens per chat request" — maps to
95: > `streamText.maxOutputTokens`, NOT a run budget. Server caps
96: > (`AGENT_MAX_STEPS` etc.) remain hard ceilings.
97: 
98: ## Best placement reasoning
99: - Workspace is the right scope: keys belong to a workspace, reusable in the
100:   `PERSONAL` workspace and future ones. Thread-level is pointless UX (user
101:   shouldn't re-enter per thread); we allow per-thread override but never require.
102: - Server retains hard caps so a user cannot self-grant unlimited budgets.
103: - Never ship keys to client — tools run server-side (Inngest/route), so only
104:   server reads them.

(End of file - total 104 lines)
</content>

10: 
11: A persistent web-agent platform. The legacy flow:
12: 
13: ```
14: Next.js UI (hardcoded demo)
15: → tRPC router  packages/api/src/routers/agent.ts  (630 lines)
16: → WorkflowService  packages/workflow/src/services/workflow-service.ts  (1517 lines)
17: → 13 repositories → Drizzle → PostgreSQL
18:    +  Inngest functions:
19:        execution-run.ts (914 lines)   — the whole agent loop
20:        schedule-tick.ts  (143 lines)  — cron + sleep/wake
21:        notification-notifier.ts       — webhook delivery

24: Capabilities (`packages/agent`): 13 registered capabilities wrapping 6 Anakin
25: adapters (search/scrape/crawl/map/research/wire) + browser sessions + memory +
26: schedules. Approval-gated: `wireAction`, `browserSessionCreate/Rename/Delete`.

28: LLM (Groq via Vercel AI SDK `ai` v7): `runAgent` in
29: `packages/agent/src/runtime.ts` drives a single `generateText` loop with
30: `isStepCount(maxSteps)` and the SDK's `toolApproval` gate. Plans and runtime
31: decisions are extracted from the model's final text with `/\`\`\`json...\`\`\`/`
32: regex in `packages/inngest/src/functions/execution-run.ts:48`.

34: Re-architecture already decided in `internal/plans/2026-09-10-aevryn-rearchitecture/`
35: and `internal/ALL-DECISIONS.md`:
36: thread === workflow, first message ≠ objective, planning output =
37: `AskUserQuestion[]` (MCQ), chat streams in the web app via `POST /api/chat`
38: (`useChat` + zod tools `askUserQuestion` / `showPlan` / `finalizeAndInject`),
39: ONE Inngest `execution/run` event only on plan approval, Supabase Auth,
40: mem0 per-thread memory. `apps/web/src/app/workspace/[threadId]/page.tsx` is the
41: empty stub that must become this.

45: ## 2. NEWTODO inventory (the user's own work order)
46: 
47: | # | File:line | Ask |
48: |---|---|---|
49: | 1 | `packages/auth/README.md:1` | Rebuild auth — Supabase Google signup ONLY |

65: ## 3. Confirmed breakages (behind "cron not working", "AI SDK not working")
66: 
67: 1. **`schedule-tick` has no trigger and is never served.**
68:    `packages/inngest/src/functions/schedule-tick.ts:21-25` declares
69:    `inngest.createFunction({ id: "schedule-tick", retries: 2 }, ...)` with no
70:    `triggers` array, and `apps/web/src/app/api/inngest/route.ts:9` registers
71:    ONLY `executionRun`. Result: cron jobs, sleep→wake, and due-work sweeping
72:    can never fire. This is the root cause of "cron broken".
73: 
74: 2. **`notificationNotifier` is also never served.** `notification/publish`
75:    events (`execution-run.ts:763`) are dropped at the SDK boundary → webhook
76:    notifications and anywhere-outside-the-app delivery are dead.
77: 
78: 3. **`resumeWorkflow` does nothing useful.**
79:    `workflow-service.ts:1024` flips `paused → active` but never enqueues a new
80:    execution or sends `execution/run`. A "resumed" workflow sits idle forever.
81: 
82: 4. **Orphaned executions on event-send failure.** Every mutator in
83:    `agent.ts` (`sendMessage`, `confirmWorkflow`, `updateObjective`,
84:    `runWorkflow`, `resolveApproval`) follows
85:    `enqueueMessage() → inngest.send()` and on send error calls
86:    `failExecution()`, but the row created by `enqueueMessage` stays
87:    `pending`. If `inngest.send` throws after enqueue, nothing ever processes
88:    that execution → permanent orphan. This send+fail block is copy-pasted 5×
89:    and is the prime candidate to kill when `/api/chat` takes over.
90: 
91: 5. **Decision parsing is regex over free-text.** `extractPlan`/`extractDecision`
92:    (`execution-run.ts:48`) parse a fenced ```json block out of the model's
93:    final message. Fragile by design and contradicts AGENTS.md rule 8/9/10
94:    (structured schemas, no free-text control). The re-architecture replaces it
95:    with real SDK tool calls. Same for `planning.ts:21` (JSON-in-prose).
96: 
97: 6. **Cost budget is post-hoc, not bound.** `runAgentStep` checks
98:    `result.usage.costUsd > EXECUTION_MAX_COST_USD` AFTER the whole run completes
99:    (`execution-run.ts:594`). It can never stop a run from overspending, it only
100:    schedules a recovery afterwards.
101: 
102: 7. **`replayedToolOutputs` is keyed by tool name** (`runtime.ts:160`) and
103:    consumed once. Fine for the single-retry case, but two capabilities with the
104:    same name would collide; also replay happens before the response cap, so a
105:    huge persisted output can refill context.
106: 
107: 8. **`GROQ_MODEL` default is `openai/gpt-oss-20b`** (`packages/env/src/server.ts:35`).
108:    Verify this exact model id exists on Groq — if the dev was running a local
109:    override this default may 404 in production. `MEM0_API_KEY` defaults to `""`
110:    (silent no-op backend).
111: 
112: 9. **`resumeWorkflow` + pause semantics.** `pauseWorkflow` cancels live
113:    executions (`workflow-service.ts:985`) and flips workflow to "paused";
114:    schedules are NOT disabled on pause (they just no-op while paused). See #3.
115: 
116: 10. **No `/api/chat`, no realtime.** The workspace renders a fully hardcoded
117:     conversation (`workspace/page.tsx`, 567 lines: mock `questions`,
118:     `workflowApproval`, accordion plan, tool-step cards, table). `trpc` client
119:     exists (`apps/web/src/utils/trpc.ts`) but nothing in workspace calls it.

124: ## 4. Architecture / data-model observations
125: 
126: - **`WorkflowService` is a 66-public-method god class** spanning every domain
127:   concept (workflow, execution, steps, state, schedule, approval, notification,

133:   Harmless at runtime, misleading to readers, and the new schema should drop it.
134: - **IDs:** domain tables use `text("id")` PKs and `@aevryn/db` `ids.*` /
135:   `isValidId`. Verify every new table gets a prefixed ULID and that
136:   `ID_PREFIXES` in `packages/db/src/ids.ts` stays in sync with the AGENTS.md
137:   prefix list (wf_/exe_/step_/tool_/mem_/evt_/rec_).

1: # DB — NEW Schema (Supabase + Drizzle)
2: 
3: Design targets (from plan): thread === workflow (1:1 after bind), chat-first,
4: PERSONAL auto workspace, MVP single-workspace (scalable), durable chat + queued
5: messages, binding approvals, plans with steps, activities/tool streaming for
6: ThinkingSteps, per-workspace API keys, mem0 thread memory, files in Supabase
7: Storage, realtime notifications, **collaboration** (workspace membership +
8: thread sharing, see ARCHITECTURE §I Permission model).
9: 
10: ## Conventions
11: - Every table: `id text primary key` (ULID via `packages/db/src/ids.ts`,
12:   prefixes `thd_`, `wf_`, `msg_`, `run_`, `pln_`, `pls_`, `apv_`, `not_`, `key_`,
13:   `fil_`, `wp_`, `grp_`, `inv_`, `tco_`, `wme_`, `alm_`), `created_at timestamptz not null default
14:   now()`, `updated_at`.
15: - All plaintext user data (API keys, secrets) NEVER stored — use Supabase Vault
16:   or encrypted column (see `workspace_api_keys`).
17: - RLS on every user table: `to authenticated using ( owner = auth.uid() )`
18:   (+ `with check` on update). Owner column is almost always `user_id`.
19: - text enums via Postgres `enum` types; drizzle maps to TS unions.
20: 
21: ## Tables
22: 
23: ### 1. `workspaces`
24: | col | type | notes |
25: |---|---|---|
26: | id | text pk | `wp_` prefix |
27: | name | text not null | e.g. "Personal" |
28: | created_by | uuid not null ref auth.users | |
29: | is_default | bool not null default false | PERSONAL per-user |
30: | created_at / updated_at | | |
31: Index: `(created_by, name)` unique.
32: RLS: owner only.
33: > MVP: auto-created "Personal" per user (is_default). Users can ALSO be added
34: > as members to OTHER workspaces via workspace invites — those workspaces show
35: > in the switcher (badge if not owner). Creating extra own-workspaces is a
36: > pro/future feature (plan limits: free = 1 owned, 3 groups, 5 threads/group).
37: 
38: ### 2. `groups`  ← sidebar folder of threads (the "group" concept)
39: | col | type | notes |
40: |---|---|---|
41: | id | text pk `grp_` |
42: | workspace_id | text ref workspaces cascade |
43: | user_id | uuid ref auth.users | creator |
44: | name | text not null | PERSONAL, SITE, WORKFLOWS, INVITES, user-created groups… |
45: | kind | enum(custom, system) default custom | system = PERSONAL/SITE/WORKFLOWS/INVITES |
46: | position | int default 0 |
47: | created_at / updated_at |
48: Unique (workspace_id, name). Indexes: (workspace_id, position).
49: RLS: owner OR member. Readable to user when owner or workspace member.
50: > **INVITES is a REAL system group** created at signup (with PERSONAL, SITE,
51: > WORKFLOWS). It is LOCKED: cannot be renamed/deleted, user cannot manually add
52: > a thread to it. It only gets populated when the user ACCEPTS a thread invite;
53: > then the owner's thread appears there. Guest cannot add anything to INVITES
54: > unless invited.
55: 
56: ### 3. `workspace_members`  ← who is in the workspace (owner/editor/viewer)
57: | col | type | notes |
58: |---|---|---|
59: | id | text pk `wme_` |
60: | workspace_id | text ref workspaces on delete cascade |
61: | user_id | uuid ref auth.users |
62: | role | enum(owner, editor, viewer) default viewer |
63: | created_at |
64: Unique (workspace_id, user_id). Creator auto-inserted as `owner` by trigger.
65: RLS: owner manages (CUD); members SELECT.
66: > Joined workspace = access to the OWNER's real workspace (all groups + threads
67: > visible to every member). Roles: owner=full, editor=work (create/edit/run/
68: > delete any thread/group, edit plans), viewer=read-only. NO owner/admin/member.
69: 
70: ### 4. `user_profiles`
71: | col | type | notes |
72: |---|---|---|
73: | id | text pk `prf_` |

276: ## Enums (Postgres)
277: ```
278: role            : owner|editor|viewer          (workspace_members)
279: thread_role     : editor|viewer                (thread_shares / invites; no owner row — owner = threads.user_id)
280: plan            : free|pro
281: group_kind      : custom|system
282: invite_kind     : workspace|thread
283: invite_status   : pending|accepted|revoked|expired
284: workflow_status : waiting|planning|running|awaiting_approval|idle|paused|failed|completed
285: message_role    : user|assistant|system|tool
286: message_status  : queued|streaming|completed|failed|interrupted
287: run_status      : pending|running|sleeping|waiting|awaiting_approval|completed|failed|cancelled
288: activity_status : pending|active|complete|failed
289: activity_type   : tool|thinking|task|subtask|system
290: approval_status : pending|approved|denied
291: api_provider    : groq|anakin|mem0|image|speech|transcription|video
292: ```
293: 
294: ## Supabase specifics
295: - Migrations via `supabase migration new <name>` (imperative workflow).
296: - **Realtime**: enable on `chat_messages`, `run_activities`,
297:   `approval_requests`, `notifications` with private channels + JWT auth.
298: - **Storage bucket**: `chat-attachments` — create server-side w/ service role;
299:   dedicated policy `(storage.foldername(name))[1] = auth.uid()::text` for
300:   CUD. Policy for avatar/object keys too.
301: - **RLS policy list**:
302:   - owner-only tables: user_profiles, notifications, workspace_api_keys,
303:     files (+ own invites).
304:   - workspace-scoped: workspaces, groups, threads, workflows, plans,
305:     chat_messages, runs, run_activities, approval_requests → readable by owner
306:     OR any `workspace_members` row (all threads visible to members).
307:   - cross-workspace thread access: `threads` also readable via a matching
308:     `thread_shares` row (invitee; in their OWN workspace context / INVITES
309:     group). Never bundled into a shared-workspace read.
310:   - `workspace_api_keys`: SELECT only via `security definer` RPC
311:     `get_workspace_key(workspace_id, provider)` that validates <owner OR
312:     workspace_members> and decrypts server-side (service role decrypt NOT
313:     exposed). Member key resolution honors `user_profiles.prefer_own_keys_in_shared`
314:     → falls back to the member's OWN Personal workspace keys.
315: - **Oracle triggers**: `on_auth_user_created` → insert
316:   `workspaces(Personal)` (is_default) + `user_profiles` row +
317:   `workspace_members(owner)` for that workspace + system `groups`
318:   (PERSONAL, SITE, WORKFLOWS, INVITES — INVITES locked empty) automatically.
319: 
320: ## Why this shape (reasoning)
321: - `threads` + `workflows` split: a chat exists before any plan/bind; binding
322:   sets `threads.bound_workflow_id`. MVP single-workspace but multi-thread.
323: - `groups` = the sidebar folder concept the plan asks for (New button → new
324:   custom group; INVITES is a LOCKED system group created at signup — empty
325:   until a thread invite is accepted). Group/thread limits (≤5 threads/group,
326:   ≤3 custom groups/workspace free) enforced at insert.
327: - `invites` unified (workspace | thread) keeps one token/status/expiry flow;
328:   accept fans out to `workspace_members` or `thread_shares`.
329: - `thread_shares` = invited guests only; role editor/viewer — guests get chat/
330:   run/approve but never plan-edit/rename/re-share (owner-only rights stay on
331:   `threads.user_id`).
332: - `runs` separate from workflow status: each durable pass is auditable,
333:   replayable, cancellable; activity tables hang off `run_id`.
334: - `run_activities` replaces old `event`/`observation`/`agent_state` — shaped
335:   directly for the ThinkingSteps/ToolStep UI components and realtime push,
336:   killing the god-table smell.
337: - `chat_messages` owns history (requirement: no hardcoded mock); queue solved
338:   by `status=queued` rows — durable across page close/reload.
339: - Plain user-supplied keys isolated in ONE table (never in env, never client)
340:   → the "Agent/Environment" dialog writes here.

(End of file - total 340 lines)

## Drizzle CAN do policies — but NOT triggers/realtime/storage

**Confirmed in your drizzle-orm 0.45.2:**
- `pgPolicy()` + `.enableRLS()` on every table ✅
- Roles via `drizzle-orm/supabase` (`authenticatedRole`, `anonRole`, `authUid`) ✅
- What's currently hand-written in tables/enums/indexes/FKs → already covered by generated `0001` ✅

**NOT possible in drizzle (no API in 0.45.2):**
- Triggers (`pgTrigger` is still an unmerged PR) → `on_auth_user_created`, limits triggers
- Realtime publications, storage bucket + policies

## Plan

**1. Delete** `20260911120000_new_schema.sql` (all 3 of its DDL blocks are now in generated `0001`).

**2. Move RLS policies into the drizzle schema (TS).** Each table file gets `.enableRLS()` + `pgPolicy` entries using `authenticatedRole` + `authUid`. DRY predicates live as shared `sql` fragments in a new `src/schema/policies.ts` (no DB-side helper functions → no ordering problem, fully drizzle-managed, Supabase idiom).

**3. `drizzle.config.ts`:** add `entities: { roles: { provider: "supabase" } }`.

**4. Regenerate** → a second migration `0002_rls` emitting only `ALTER TABLE ... ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` + `CREATE POLICY ...` (tables already in 0001, nothing destroyed).

**5. ONE minimal raw SQL** `supabase/migrations/9900_supabase_glue.sql` — the genuinely non-drizzle parts only:
- `handle_new_user()` + `on_auth_user_created` trigger
- Limit triggers (threads/group, groups/workspace) + system-group protection
- Realtime publications (chat_messages, run_activities, approval_requests, notifications)
- `chat-attachments` storage bucket + policies
